title: finding(react): useOffline's auto-sync drains one batch and leaves the remainder until the next transition
body:
Noticed while implementing objectui#6818 (auto-sync guarding on a stale queue).
Deliberately **not** folded into that fix, and the reason is the point of this
card: closing it is not a bug fix, it is a decision about what `batchSize` means.

## What

After objectui#6818 the auto-sync effect is keyed on the boolean
`queue.length > 0`, which is what keeps the 100ms stabilization timer from
restarting once per queued mutation. One consequence follows from the boolean
and is written into the code comment there rather than hidden:

- queue holds 5 mutations, `sync: { batchSize: 2 }`, online;
- the timer fires, `sync()` flushes 2, the queue drops to 3;
- `queue.length > 0` was true before and is still true, so the effect does not
  re-run and no second timer is armed;
- the remaining 3 wait for the next transition — an `isOnline` / `enabled`
  change, or the queue reaching empty and refilling.

This is the pre-existing behaviour, not a regression: before objectui#6818 the
same remainder was stranded (and so was everything else queued while online).
The fix strictly reduced the stranded set; it did not empty it.

## The actual question

Should ONE auto-sync drain the whole queue batch-by-batch, or one batch?

- **One batch** is what `batchSize`'s docstring says today — "Mutations flushed
  per sync batch" — and it matches the manual API, where a caller invokes
  `sync()` again for the next batch.
- **Drain to empty** is what "auto-sync" implies to a reader, and it is what
  makes the queue self-clearing without a consumer loop.

Both are defensible and they are not the same product. A shape that closes it
without reintroducing the per-mutation timer restart exists — key the effect on
the id of the queue's head (`queue[0]?.id`) instead of on the boolean: it is
unchanged when a mutation is appended, and changes when a batch drains, so it
re-arms exactly once per drained batch. That is offered as evidence the option
is cheap, **not** as a recommendation: it turns `batchSize` into the chunk size
of a repeating 100ms-spaced drain loop against a published hook whose
out-of-repo population is unmeasured.

## Blast radius

`useOffline` has one in-repo consumer, `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx:132`,
which destructures `isOnline` only — nothing in this repo reaches the sync queue.
It is a published hook, so anything outside is unmeasured.

No user-visible break is measured and none is claimed.

## Dedupe

`/search/issues` returns silent zeros for this seat, so this went through the
repo-scoped REST list endpoint plus a local grep: 247 open issues collected,
one hit for `batchSize` (objectui#6818 itself) and one for `useOffline` (also
objectui#6818), zero for `syncState` or `pendingCount`. Control terms hit in the
same read (`hook` matched 15 issues, `useETagCache` matched objectui#6817,
`offline` matched objectui#6818), so the zero is a real reading.
